button.label: Run script
button.screentip: Run a script of the library
button.supertip: Lists the .vas files of the library folder and runs the one you pick. A script whose header asks for the selection gets the selected range as $1.

button.label: Library folder
button.supertip: The folder of the scripts that ASF_CALL and Run script use, and the only folder imports read.

button.label: Why this error?
button.screentip: Why ASF_RUN, ASF_CALL or a Python function gave an error
button.supertip: Calculates the active cell again and shows the message of its ASF_RUN or ASF_CALL, or the Python error and traceback of its PY_CALL or Python function when the Python add-in is loaded.

button.label: Reset engine
button.screentip: Reset the engine of the worksheet functions
button.supertip: Drops the compiled scripts and reads the settings again on the next formula.

button.label: Python studio
button.screentip: Write and run Python for Excel
button.supertip: An editor for the modules of the Python folder, with completions and problems as you type; saving reloads them in Excel. Run a module in Excel, run the macros, see the functions Excel gets, and install or upgrade packages.

button.label: Python console
button.screentip: The add-in's Python at its prompt
button.supertip: A console window with the Python of the Python add-in, apart from Excel: pip("install numpy") manages the packages, and the modules of the Python folder import, to try a package or a function before Excel loads it.

button.label: Python settings
button.screentip: Choose the Python, the Python folder and PythonAccess
button.supertip: Which Python the Python add-in runs (its own, or a venv or install), the folder of your Python modules, and what library scripts may do with Python. Excel needs a restart for the first two.

button.label: Python updates
button.screentip: The add-in's version and its updates
button.supertip: Which version of the Python add-in runs, whether a newer one is out, and installing it; and whether Excel looks for one when it starts (PythonUpdates). Opens the Add-in page of Python studio.

button.label: About Python
button.supertip: The loaded Python add-in and its version, its Python, the settings, what the Python folder gave at start-up, and the log, to open.
